[p39] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Traffic Control › Signs › Red YIELD Sign · ¶1 | para
Slow down and be ready to stop to let any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian pass before you proceed.

[p40] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Traffic Control › Signs › Yellow and Black Circular Sign or X-shaped Sign · ¶1 | para
You are approaching a railroad crossing. Look, listen, slow down, and prepare to stop. Let any trains pass before you proceed.

[p41] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Traffic Control › Signs › White Rectangular Sign · ¶1 | para
Communicates many important rules you must obey.

[p42] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Traffic Control › Signs › Warning Signs · image | figure
Figure: Alt text: “Examples of Red and White Regulatory Signs, White Regulatory Signs, Highway Construction and Maintenance Signs, Guide Signs, Hazardous Loads Placards, and Slow Moving Vehicle Placard”

[p43] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First? › Roundabouts · ¶2 | para
How to use a roundabout:

[p44] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First? › Roundabouts · item 5 | step
Travel in a counter-clockwise direction. Do not stop or pass.

[p45] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First? › Pedestrians · ¶5 | para
Other things to keep in mind:

[p46] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First? › Pedestrians · item 4 | item
Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. You may not be able to see a pedestrian crossing the street.

[p47] page: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road | heading: Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First? › Mountain Roads · ¶1 | para
If two vehicles meet on a steep narrow road and neither vehicle can pass, the vehicle facing uphill has the right-of-way. The vehicle facing downhill has more control when backing up the hill. The vehicle facing downhill should back up until the vehicle going uphill can pass.
